source_reviews.independent_solution: With the rider, bicycle, posture and gearing fixed, still air makes faster steady riding a larger air-relative speed. Increased air drag raises the opposing load while the stipulated rolling/mechanical losses remain approximately unchanged. Steady motion requires balanced external forces; greater effective pedal torque is transmitted to the driven wheel, whose forward ground traction balances the external load. Mechanical losses affect input torque, not an additional external force on the whole bicycle. Tire-ground static friction is not a fixed resisting loss. Greater power at greater speed does not alone imply greater force, and no precise linear/quadratic drag law is implied. Recorded before learner options in source-blind.md.
